title: Raising Children in the Lord
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Raising children in the Lord means nurturing, instructing, correcting, loving, and discipling children according to God’s Word. Parents are called to shepherd children toward the Lord, not merely manage behavior or secure worldly success.
summary: Raising children in the Lord means nurturing, instructing, correcting, loving, and discipling children according to God’s Word. Parents are called to shepherd children toward the Lord, not merely manage behavior or secure worldly success.
christFocus: Jesus Christ welcomes children and calls families to bring the young under His truth and care. Children need more than rules; they need to hear of Christ, grace, repentance, faith, and obedience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Children are to be raised with instruction and discipline of the Lord. Parents are not called merely to produce outwardly successful children, but to teach God’s truth faithfully.

Discipleship in the home is daily and ordinary. God’s Word is to be spoken in the rhythms of life, forming memory, worship, wisdom, and obedience.

Parents must also guard against provoking and discouraging children. Correction without love can crush. Love without truth can mislead. Children need patient instruction shaped by grace and holiness.

Only God can save, but parents are responsible to teach, pray, model repentance, and point children to Christ. The home is one of the first places doctrine becomes visible.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many parents feel overwhelmed or guilty. This doctrine does not call for perfection, but faithful dependence on God. Children need parents who repent, pray, teach, love, and keep pointing them to Jesus.

It also protects against outsourcing discipleship completely. Church teaching matters, but parents still carry a primary calling to teach God’s Word in the home.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Teach children the Word of God with patience and consistency. Pray with them, explain the Gospel, correct sin lovingly, confess your own failures, and show them what repentance and faith look like. Aim not merely at control, but at discipleship under Christ.
